newsitem.title: UK: British Aerospace up in pre-market trade.
newsitem.headline: British Aerospace up in pre-market trade.

text.p: Shares in British Aerospace Plc rose one penny to 1126-1/2p in pre-market trade on Monday after news on Sunday of a merger between its two U.S. competitors.
Rivals Boeing Co and McDonnell Douglas announced a $13.3 billion merger plan over the weekend which would create the world's largest aerospace firm, dwarfing European aircraft consortium Airbus.
Airbus is made up of Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
Despite the early rise in the share price, aerospace analysts were pessimistic about the short-term prospects for British Aerospace.

Contributing to the negative tone, an article in Monday's Financial Times reported that France's Aerospatiale was at odds with BAe and Daimler Benz Aerospace over proposals for Airbus to take control of manufacturing at its member sites.
"On balance the news today is clearly negative and I expect BAe to go down," said BZW industry analyst Nick Cunningham. "I don't think it will really perform again until Lagardere get Thomson."
"That's what we need to get it back to positive territory," Cunningham added.

Earlier this month the French government pulled the plug on the sale of defence electronics firm Thomson CSF to Lagardere Group after objections to Lagardere selling the rest of Thomson SA to Korea's Daewoo Electronics.
